extracted.subtask_description: Wartime newspaper dispatches and front‑page news items reporting military operations, political developments and home‑front measures; includes agency datelines and statements about censorship and distribution conditions. The implicit production standards concern attribution, verification, censorship compliance, and distribution constraints for overseas editions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dateline and wire/agency attribution
rubrics_metrics.description: Each item carries a dateline (city, date) and an agency indicator (e.g., London, Feb. 21 (A. P.), London, Feb. 21 (P)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Begin dispatches with a clear dateline and identify the news agency or correspondent. This signals the source and timeliness of the report and follows examples such as 'London, Feb. 21 (A. P.)' and 'London, Tuesday, Feb. 22 (P)'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Attribute numeric casualty and capture figures to their source
rubrics_metrics.description: Casualty/strength numbers and territorial claims are reported with explicit attribution (e.g., 'The Russians have announced the erasure of the trap, with 73,200 Germans declared killed or captured.'; 'The announcement said ... 90,000 Russians had been killed during the last month’s fighting').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When publishing large figures or battlefield tallies, state clearly who made the claim (Moscow announcements, Berlin broadcasts, etc.) and avoid presenting such numbers as independently verified facts without that attribution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mark enemy or third‑party claims as unconfirmed when appropriate
rubrics_metrics.description: Enemy or propaganda claims are often reported alongside a qualification of their status (example: 'The Berlin radio reported today that German submarines had sunk 11 Allied escort destroyers ... The claim was wholly without confirmation.').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a claim cannot be corroborated, explicitly flag it as unconfirmed or lacking independent verification rather than repeating it unqualified; this prevents misleading readers and distinguishes assertion from confirmed fact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use and identification of official broadcasts/monitored communiqués as sources
rubrics_metrics.description: Material from official radio broadcasts and monitored communiqués is used and identified (e.g., 'The communique, broadcast by the Moscow radio and recorded by the Soviet monitor here').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When using government radio broadcasts or monitored communiques, report that the item was broadcast and, where applicable, that it was recorded by a monitor. Make clear the route by which the information reached the reporter (broadcast, monitor recording, press agency).

rubrics_metrics.name: Comply with wartime censorship restrictions (omit prohibited details)
rubrics_metrics.description: The text notes explicit censorship rules that constrain reporting (example: 'British censorship forbids advance mention in dispatches of the date set for any Commons session.').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Obey applicable wartime censorship orders: omit or withhold details specifically barred (such as advance dates of government sessions) and be aware that security rules may require leaving out information even when it is newsworthy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Withhold names until next‑of‑kin notification when required
rubrics_metrics.description: The article states that the names of service members cannot be released 'until their next of kin are notified.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not publish the names of casualties or severely wounded personnel until official next‑of‑kin notification procedures have been completed. Clearly state when names are being withheld for this reason.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distribution conditions for overseas weekly editions to troops
rubrics_metrics.description: Permission to distribute weekly overseas editions to American troops comes with specific conditions: 'The conditions specify that the newspapers are not to be ... than eight pages, 12ate inches, with the number of copies [to meet] the demand, and the sale price to be set ... by the Exchange Service.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When preparing newspapers for overseas military distribution, comply with prescribed format and distribution rules (page limits, physical dimensions where specified, copy allocation to meet demand, and sale price set by the Exchange Service). Explicitly follow any conditions set by military authorities.
